'''Dewan Hernandez''' (born Dewan Huell on December 9, 1996) is an American [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]] in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC).

==High school career==
Huell attended [[Miami Norland Senior High School|Miami Norland High School]] in [[Miami, Florida]], playing on three state championship teams. As a senior, he averaged 19.2 points and 9.1 rebounds per game and was the Miami Herald 8A-6A Player of the Year. In January 2016, Huell was named a McDonald's All American, and competed in the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Game]].<ref name="herald">{{cite news|last1=Kaufman|first1=Michelle|title=Cops say top UM basketball recruit assaulted man hiding with ex-girlfriend|url=http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-miami/article101773392.html#1|accessdate=December 5, 2017|work=[[Miami Herald]]|date=September 14, 2016}}</ref> In the Under Armour Association circuit, Huell participated with Team Breakdown and averaged 16.1 points and 8.6 rebounds per game. He committed to Miami after considering offers from [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] and [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Johnson|first1=Chris|title=Miami gets another elite recruit in five-star big man Dewan Huell|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/11/18/dewan-huell-commits-miami-hurricanes-bruce-brown|accessdate=December 5, 2017|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=November 18, 2015}}</ref> Huell was rated as a five-star recruit and was ranked 28th in the 2016 high school class by [[ESPN]].

==College career==
In September 2016, Huell was arrested after breaking into his girlfriend's dorm room at [[Florida International University]]. According to police, he forcefully dragged a male visitor out of the room, leaving him with scratches on his chest.<ref name="herald"/> Despite the assault charge, Huell did not miss any playing time for the Hurricanes.<ref name="wont">{{cite news|title=Miami freshman Dewan Huell won't be suspended|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/17601070/dewan-huell-miami-hurricanes-suspended-arrest|accessdate=December 5, 2017|work=[[ESPN]]|date=September 21, 2016}}</ref> As a freshman, he averaged 5.8 points and 3.1 rebounds per game. He showed marked improvement as a sophomore and scored a career-high 23 points in a victory over [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]] on November 29, 2017.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Kaufman|first1=Michelle|title=Sophomore has career night as Hurricanes stay unbeaten with close win on the road|url=http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-miami/article187330413.html|accessdate=December 5, 2017|work=[[Miami Herald]]|date=November 30, 2017}}</ref> Huell averaged 11.4 points and 6.6 rebounds per game as a sophomore while shooting 57 percent from the field. Following the season, he declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]] but did not hire an agent and ultimately withdrew and returned to Miami.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Phillips |first1=Scott |title=Dewan Huell returning to Miami for junior season |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2018/05/26/dewan-huell-returning-to-miami-for-junior-season/ |accessdate=May 30, 2018 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=May 26, 2018}}</ref>

In October 2018 he announced he had legally changed his name to Dewan Hernandez in honor of his mother, Christina Hernandez.<ref>{{cite news |title=Hurricanes forward Dewan Huell changes name to Hernandez |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2018/10/10/hurricanes-forward-dewan-huell-changes-name-to-hernandez/ |accessdate=October 12, 2018 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=October 10, 2018}}</ref> Hernandez ultimately would not play for Miami in his junior season due to eligibility concerns relating to the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal]] revolving around Christian Dawkins.<ref>http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/25683869/miami-hurricanes-weigh-options-ncaa-rejects-dewan-hernandez-appeal-eligibility</ref> After failing to qualify for eligibility twice,<ref>http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/25762606/dewan-hernandez-miami-hurricanes-hopes-play-ncaa-committee-upholds-previous-rulings</ref> Hernandez declared his entry for the [[2019 NBA Draft]] on January 28, 2019.<ref>https://twitter.com/DewanGoesFor_20/status/1089991097521238016</ref>
